title: Build a Human Classifier
outcome: By the end, I can build a complete classifier that validates inputs before predicting.
scenario: A fictional ribbon sorter uses a fixed instruction card called RibbonR.
given: Valid input: whole-number length from 0 to 15 with unit cm.
Predict long at least 9 cm; otherwise short. Missing, wrong-unit or out-of-range values request clarification.

steps.label: Input contract
steps.detail: Check that length is present, whole, within 0–15, and in cm.

steps.label: Invalid cases
steps.detail: 16 cm and blank length → clarification, not a forced label.

steps.label: Keep records
steps.detail: Store input, contract result, rule version and prediction.

explanation: A prediction boundary answers a different question from input validation. Length 9 passes the contract and meets the long boundary. Length 16 must not receive long merely because it exceeds 9: it violates the allowed range first. Zero is permitted and receives short.

counterfactual.prediction: Request clarification rather than predicting long.
counterfactual.reason: RibbonR requires cm; the unit mismatch fails its declared input contract.

student_task: Trace 0 cm and explain why clarification is different from predicting short.
teacher_answer: 0 is a valid whole-number centimetre input, so RibbonR predicts short. Clarification means no supported prediction was made because required input checks failed.
project_evidence: Create a sorter instruction card covering valid values, equality, missing fields and who can resolve clarification requests.
limits: Contract validity does not prove the predicted category agrees with a checked reference label.
review_note: New fictional worked case reviewed against the weekly topic and reserved independent assessment. Keep that assessment separate; this picture is supported practice.
